note: NECO Literature round 6 (R44 top-up): 13 fresh author-work pairs (People of the City; Old Man and the Sea; Paradise Lost; Anowa; Dilemma of a Ghost; Potter's Wheel; Second-Class Citizen; The Stillborn; Once Upon Four Robbers; Americanah; So Long a Letter; Kongi's Harvest; Our Husband Has Gone Mad Again) plus poetic licence; eponymous; dumb show; improvisation; props; doggerel; poetic diction; lullaby; work song; magic realism; utopia; slapstick. Scanned against the whole Literature pool (JAMB, WAEC and NECO stems).

questions.q: Ama Ata Aidoo's first play, in which the student Ato Yawson returns from America with a Black American wife, is

questions.q: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's novel in which Ifemelu returns to Nigeria after years in America, famous for her blog on race, is

questions.q: In Wole Soyinka's play, the military ruler President Kongi awaits the new-yam festival that will crown his power over the kingdom of Isma. The play is

questions.q: Ola Rotimi's comedy in which the retired Major Lejoka-Brown throws himself into election politics with disastrous results is
questions.B: Our Husband Has Gone Mad Again
questions.C: If: A Tragedy of the Ruled

questions.subject: Literature-in-English
questions.q: The freedom a poet or novelist allows himself to bend facts and break ordinary rules for the sake of artistic effect is called
questions.explanation: Art may stretch truth where plain record may not.

questions.subject: Literature-in-English
questions.q: A work named after its main character, as Oliver Twist is named after the orphan boy, is said to be
questions.explanation: The hero's own name stands on the title page.

questions.q: A short dramatic scene performed entirely in silence, without any spoken words, is called a

questions.explanation: The scene is born fresh at every performance.

questions.explanation: The actor picks them up and uses them on stage.

questions.q: Light verse of rough, careless rhythm, written for laughter rather than for serious art, is called
questions.explanation: Its clumsy lines are loved for their fun.

questions.subject: Literature-in-English
questions.q: The special, often elevated choice of words and phrasing that belongs to poetry rather than to everyday speech is called
questions.explanation: Poets dress ideas in words beyond daily talk.

questions.subject: Literature-in-English
questions.q: A soft, rocking song sung by a mother to soothe her baby to sleep is a
questions.explanation: Its gentle rhythm nods the child off to sleep.

questions.q: A song sung in rhythm by workers at a shared task, such as paddling a canoe or pounding cassava, to make the labour lighter is a
questions.explanation: The beat of the song sets the pace of the work.

questions.subject: Literature-in-English
questions.q: A style of fiction in which spirits and the living mix as a matter of course, as in Ben Okri's The Famished Road, is called
questions.explanation: The spirit world walks in without any surprise.

questions.q: An imagined perfect society, in which everything is arranged for the good of all, is called a

questions.q: Broad physical comedy built on falls, chases, collisions and harmless beatings is called
